title: At the front door
intro: You reach the door. Everyone’s already inside, talking.
label: Go in the front door
choice1_text: Walk in and join in like everything’s normal
choice1_pro: Feels easy — no explaining, nothing to perform.
choice1_con: What’s on your mind is still there — just unsaid.
choice1_tip: Find a later moment — don’t let ’later’ become ’never’.
choice2_text: Say what’s actually on your mind
choice2_pro: Genuinely brave — saying it beats carrying it alone.
choice2_con: Can feel exposed for a second. Normal, and it passes fast.
choice2_tip: Try: ’can I tell you something?’ — it opens the space first.
choice3_text: Go straight to your room instead
choice3_pro: You got the space you needed. A real, valid choice.
choice3_con: No one knows why — might look like something’s wrong.
choice3_tip: One line on the way past — ’just need a minute’ — closes the gap.

title: Around the side
intro: You see it first — something’s broken, and it was you.
label: Around the side, past the gate
choice1_text: Tell someone straight away, before it’s found
choice1_pro: Strongest option — you said it, you weren’t caught.
choice1_con: Stomach drops right before — that’s just nerves.
choice1_tip: Try: ’I need to tell you something’ — lands as honesty.
choice2_text: Fix it quietly and say nothing
choice2_pro: Quietly putting it right, no credit needed — real character.
choice2_con: If found later, it can look hidden — even though it wasn’t.
choice2_tip: Fix it AND mention it — ’by the way, I sorted that’.
choice3_text: Wait and see if anyone notices
choice3_pro: Costs nothing right now — no hard conversation today.
choice3_con: The longer it waits, the bigger it gets when it’s found.
choice3_tip: Set a deadline — ’if I haven’t said it by tonight, I will’.

title: Staying in the garden
intro: A couple of kids pass the gate, laughing, aimed right at you.
label: Stay right here in the garden
choice1_text: Laugh along like it doesn’t bother you
choice1_pro: Can genuinely take the wind out of it.
choice1_con: It still landed inside — laughing along just hides the sting.
choice1_tip: Fine to look okay AND tell someone about it after.
choice2_text: Say something back to match them
choice2_pro: Standing your ground has real value.
choice2_con: Usually exactly what they wanted — it can escalate fast.
choice2_tip: One flat word — ’okay’ — does the job, feeds nothing.
choice3_text: Stay calm, say nothing, and walk further into the garden
choice3_pro: The strongest response — nothing to feed off.
choice3_con: Letting it sit unanswered is hard. Real, not wrong.
choice3_tip: Tell someone after — calm in the moment, not silent about it.

title: One last thing
intro: On your way to bed, you pass the door. Something from earlier is still sitting with you — unsaid.
label: Go back to the door
choice1_text: Go say it now, even though it’s late
choice1_pro: Sleep without carrying it too — worth ten minutes.
choice1_con: Bedtime’s odd timing — but there’s rarely a perfect one.
choice1_tip: Short version works — ’one more thing before I go up’.
choice2_pro: Sleep helps — morning-you often handles it better.
choice2_con: ’Tomorrow’ can quietly become ’never’ once the moment’s gone.
choice2_tip: Pick an actual time tomorrow — not just ’sometime’.
choice3_text: Write it down instead, for now
choice3_pro: Gets it out of your head — sometimes that’s the real release.
choice3_con: Doesn’t tell them anything — the gap stays the same.
choice3_tip: Keep the note somewhere you’ll actually see tomorrow.

title: Lying there
intro: You get into bed. The room’s quiet. Today replays a little in your head.
label: Get into bed
choice1_text: Think about what you’d do the same again
choice1_pro: Noticing what worked matters as much as what didn’t.
choice1_con: Easy to skip — feels less urgent than the hard parts.
choice1_tip: Say it out loud once — ’I think I handled that alright’.
choice2_text: Think about what you might try differently
choice2_pro: This is where real growth happens.
choice2_con: Watch it doesn’t become ’I did it wrong’ — different thing.
choice2_tip: No need to act tonight. Noticing it is enough.
choice3_text: Just let it go and think about something else
choice3_pro: Completely valid — not every day needs unpacking.
choice3_con: If it’s every night, even hard ones, that’s worth noticing.
choice3_tip: Resting’s fine. Every single time is worth mentioning.

title: Still awake
intro: You look out at the moon for a minute. Your mind’s still going, even though your body’s tired.
label: Look out at the window
choice1_text: Try to think about something calm on purpose
choice1_pro: Choosing what to think about, on purpose, is a real skill.
choice1_con: Might not work first try — wandering back is normal.
choice1_tip: Picture somewhere calm in real detail — detail is what works.
choice2_text: Get up and write the thought down
choice2_pro: Once it’s on paper, your brain can let it go.
choice2_con: Breaks the winding-down feeling — you’ll need to settle again.
choice2_tip: Keep paper by the bed — keeps the interruption short.
choice3_text: Just lie there and let the thoughts keep going
choice3_pro: Thoughts sometimes run their course on their own.
choice3_con: If it’s most nights and takes ages, that’s worth noticing.
choice3_tip: If it’s most nights, tell someone — don’t figure it out alone.

title: The dinner table
intro: Dinner’s on the table. Someone asks ‘how was your day?’ — and just for a second, everyone’s actually listening.
label: Sit down at the table
choice1_con: If today wasn’t fine, this moment just quietly passed.
choice1_tip: Short now doesn’t rule out longer later — ’can I tell you after?’
choice2_text: Actually say what today was really like
choice2_pro: Say it once, to everyone — not three times later.
choice2_con: More eyes on you than planned — a real trade-off.
choice2_tip: Short version first, then ’actually, can I say more’.
choice3_text: Ask someone else about their day instead
choice3_pro: Genuinely kind — people notice being asked.
choice3_con: Your own day stays exactly where it was — unsaid.
choice3_tip: Works as a stall, not a swap — circle back to yours too.

title: Washing up
intro: Dinner’s finished. The pans are still out. Nobody’s said anything about who’s doing them.
label: Notice the washing up
choice1_text: Offer to do them without being asked
choice1_pro: Noticed more than almost anything — offering beats being told.
choice1_con: Extra effort when you’d rather be done — that’s real.
choice1_tip: Doing half and asking for help still counts.
choice2_text: Wait to see if someone asks you
choice2_pro: Resting after a meal is allowed.
choice2_con: If everyone waits, the pans just sit there.
choice2_tip: A quick ’shout if you want a hand’ covers you either way.
choice3_text: Slip off before the question even comes up
choice3_pro: Sometimes you’re genuinely done — that’s allowed.
choice3_con: If it’s the regular pattern, it’s usually noticed.
choice3_tip: ’Got to run, back in a bit’ reads differently to vanishing.
